# Good Visualisation & Tables {#sec-viz-tables}

::: {.callout-note title="Why this matters"}
Analysis & Evidence (35 points) and Report Clarity & Storytelling (20
points) — more than half of your score comes from these elements, so it's
worth looking over these materials to create good visualisation and
tables. Even solid analysis loses marks if it's shown as raw R output or a
cluttered default chart.
:::

Start from the message, not the chart: write the one-sentence finding
first, then pick the plot or table that makes it obvious. A few things
worth knowing regardless of which chart you pick, position and length
(bar charts, scatter plots) are judged far more accurately than angle and
area (pie charts), so prefer the former; sort categories by value instead
of leaving them alphabetical; and for tables, don't paste a `summary()`
printout into the report, `broom::tidy()` turns a fitted model into a data
frame, and `gtsummary::tbl_regression()` turns that into a table you can
actually trim down to what answers your question.

For the full treatment, perception, colour palettes, a worked
diagnose/redesign/evaluate example, and table-formatting details, go
through the two Monash ETC5523 (Communicating with Data) lectures this is
drawn from:

- [Week 5 — from model outputs to communicative
  tables](https://cwd.numbat.space/week5/#/etc5523-title)
- [Week 6 — effective data
  visualisation](https://cwd.numbat.space/week6/#/etc5523-title)
